tensorboard_comparison.source: existing RSL-RL events, identical update steps 96-127, 32 samples each; reward densities exclude discrete terminal events
tensorboard_comparison.legacy_axis_std_note: v3 has no per-axis std event tags; its final vector remains available in the checkpoint

trace_diagnosis.scope: three cases, one fixed representative each; state/action times 0.2/0.4/0.6 s, root pitch from preceding 4-tick body sample with its separate timestamp; descriptive, not a matched-state intervention
trace_diagnosis.body_pose_scope: representatives every four policy ticks, post-step after possible auto-reset
trace_diagnosis.interpretation: The v4 standing representative requests larger wheel correction as pitch departs and actual wheel speed follows partially; all episodes still terminate. This does not prove a unique cause or adequate closed-loop control.

interpretation: All eight case mean lifetimes increase against v3 at 128 updates, but all 32 episodes still fail by nonwheel contact. Stochastic training has 1406 closure guards and 5.494 mm maximum gap. Lower leg smoothness costs, finite states, and longer short episodes are not acceptance.

next_bounded_experiment.rationale: The 128-update deterministic lifetime improvement appears in all eight cases, training episodes rise 0.740 to 0.815 s, and the trace shows changed wheel feedback. Extend only to the same 512-update diagnostic horizon as v2/v3, then re-evaluate. Preserve reward, timing, mechanical gates and all consumption.
